answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and penalizes identities caught double-signing or coordinating fraudulent claims, so creating a nebula of aliases does not multiply voting power for free. An attacker must spread capital across accounts, keep it locked through the horizon of the challenge period, and risk losing it; the delta is a real, growing cost for each extra unit of influence.
